narrative.overview:
TadeoTTools works like an open-day programme you carry on your phone. The visitor GuideApp follows the Nachtband world of leo-projects, adapted to the phone: a night-blue frame taken from htl-leonding.at carries the logo, the page title and the way on. Each stop group carries its own progress as a bar of stops in their division colours, on its card and in its page's band, because visitors pick one guide tour rather than the whole day. Below the frame the canvas is light, and the day is a list of stop groups and stops, each a white or division-filled panel to open and tick off. The school's own division colours (Informatik blue, Medientechnik sky blue, Elektronik red, Medizintechnik amber, plus whatever the admins set) are the wayfinding signal; a glance at a card's fill tells you which part of the school you are in.

Colour is strictly distributed. Night blue is the frame and never content. Orange only marks what you can do (the "Auf der Karte" link next to the room, "Erneut versuchen"), the active tab and the focus. Status is neutral: a seen stop gets a gray-900 tick, not an orange one. Type is Manrope, the school's typeface, with one extra-bold title per page in the band. Rows are tall (at least 80px) and every tap target is at least 44px, because visitors tap while walking; body text never drops below 16px. There is one motion moment: the tour band grows in once per visit.

The organizer dashboard is the programme's back office. It uses the same rounded, lifted vocabulary at office density: DaisyUI components, 14px body text, a sky-blue palette instead of orange, and a full dark mode. Its distinctive habit is **filled blue filter fields**: the search and filter fields above a list sit in solid steel blue (`dash-field`) with white text and placeholders, while form inputs are plain bordered fields. The two apps are documented as separate sub-systems that share only the HTL Leonding logo and the division colors.
keyCharacteristics: Division colors are the identity and the wayfinding signal; they come from the school, not from the design.

GuideApp: Nachtband on the phone: a sticky night top bar and title band, a tour band per stop group, white 16px-radius panels on a light canvas, orange only for action, selection and focus, a fixed bottom tab bar.
Dashboard: DaisyUI `light` / `darkCustom` themes, blue primary, filled blue filter fields, a sticky sky-blue top nav, one left-aligned page header on every page.
Tall touch targets (44px or more in the GuideApp) and a 16px side gutter on mobile; the GuideApp is designed only for phone width.
Copy: German with du-form in the GuideApp, English in the dashboard (today's state, not a rule).

Kiosks (`kiosk/`): one shared kiosk world (Roboto, the Tailwind orange scale as the only accent, white cards lifted on a `gray-50` canvas) at tablet size. It is the GuideApp's look from before the Nachtband redesign and stays separate from it. Feedback (exit tablets) and Registration (entrance tablets) speak to the visitor, the Cashier (buffet) to the student selling; Statistics scales the same world up for the hall projector. See the four kiosk sections.

rules.name: The Division Owns Its Color Rule
rules.body: Division colors come from the school and the dashboard data. Never re-tint them, and never reuse a division hue for UI states like errors or links.

rules.name: The Untinted Identity Rule
rules.body: (GuideApp, from Nachtband) Division colours appear exactly as the admin set them, on stop cards and tour band segments. They are never tinted, darkened, faded or overlaid, not even for seen stops. One deliberate exception to Nachtband's no-gradient rule, decided by the user ("the cut is too hard"): a stop in several divisions gets a smooth left-to-right gradient through its exact colours.

rules.name: The Orange Means Act Rule
rules.body: (GuideApp, from Nachtband) Orange is only action (accent-700 buttons), selection and focus (accent-600, accent-400 on night). Never status, counts or decoration: orange sits next to Medizintechnik amber, and any other orange surface reads as a division.

rules.name: The Neutral Status Rule
rules.body: (GuideApp, from Nachtband) "Seen" is a status, so it is neutral: a gray-900 box with a white tick, a gray-500 group name, a taller tour band segment. Never orange, never a division colour, never night blue.

rules.name: The One Seen Rule
rules.body: (GuideApp) A stop is the unit of progress (`ProgressService`, `localStorage` key `finishedStops`). A group is seen when all its stops are seen; ticking a group ticks or unticks all its stops. Only a group without stops is stored as a group (`finishedStopGroups`). Cards, the "3/7" count, the tour band and the count line all read the same state, so they never disagree.

rules.name: The Night Is The Frame Rule
rules.body: (GuideApp, from Nachtband) Night blue is the top bar, the title band and the tour band track. Never a text, link or surface colour on the canvas.

rules.name: The Same White Text Rule
rules.body: (GuideApp, user decision) Stop names are white on every fill, with a soft text shadow (`0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45)`). The user chose this knowingly over a white chip or a per-fill text colour. Its known cost: white fails WCAG contrast on light fills such as HITM, HBG, ALL and ORG.

rules.name: The White Text Needs 4.5 Rule
rules.body: Any fill that carries white text in the dashboard (primary buttons, filled fields, toasts) must reach 4.5:1. That is why the primary is `#1f6fd1`, not the lighter `#4590e6`, and why status text uses the 700 shades in light mode and the 400 shades in dark mode.

rules.name: The Pending Is Not A Warning Rule
rules.body: Pending is teal, near Approved green: it means "on track, waiting for a decision". Orange is reserved for Conflict, the one state that needs the admin's attention.

rules.name: The Arm's-Length Rule
rules.body: GuideApp text is read while walking: body 18px, meta and card text at least 16px (the phone adaptation of Nachtband's 14px desktop body). The one exception is the room number on stop cards (14px medium, user decision 2026-10-12): it must sit clearly below the 18px bold name.

rules.name: The One Big Title Rule
rules.body: (GuideApp, from Nachtband) Size happens once per page: the extra-bold title in the band. Below it, emphasis is bold and gray-900, not larger.

rules.name: The Lifted Card Rule
rules.body: Anything tappable in the GuideApp is a 16px-radius panel on a soft neutral shadow. Ticking changes nothing about the card itself: it keeps its height (at least 80px), shadow, fill and full opacity, so the next row never moves (user decision).

rules.name: The Per Group Rule
rules.body: (GuideApp, user decision 2026-10-12) Most visitors pick one guide tour, so progress is never shown across the whole day: a bar over all 37 stops would tell them they never finish. Each group shows its own progress.

rules.name: The One Motion Rule
rules.body: (GuideApp, from Nachtband) The group page's tour band growing in from the left is the GuideApp's one motion moment (900ms, `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, once per group and visit, remembered in `sessionStorage`); the bands on the cards don't grow. Everything else is a short state transition. `prefers-reduced-motion` turns it and all transitions off. The band is `aria-hidden`; the count next to it carries the same information.

rules.name: The No Short Names Rule
rules.body: (GuideApp, user decision 2026-10-12) Division short names are organizer vocabulary. The GuideApp shows a division only by its colour and its icon.

dos: **Do** fill GuideApp stop cards and tour band segments with the stop's exact runtime division colour, a left-to-right gradient through the exact colours for several divisions, and No-Division Gray (`guide-no-division`) only when the stop has no division.
**Do** keep GuideApp tap targets at least 44px, list cards at least 80px, and body text at least 16px.
**Do** use Action Orange (accent-700) for the one action button on a GuideApp screen, and Selection Orange (accent-600) for the active tab and focus.
**Do** start every GuideApp page with the night frame: the 56px top bar and a title band with one extra-bold title; subpages get a back link to their parent in the band.
**Do** show "seen" neutrally in the GuideApp: the gray-900 checkbox, the gray-500 group name, the 12px tour band segment.
